title: Zoom in: a third notifier joins and only two partitions move
caption: With the cooperative protocol members keep consuming while the group rebalances; only the partitions that change owner pause.

messages.label: JoinGroup
messages.note: The misconnects topic has 6 partitions; a third notifier starts because lag is climbing.

messages.label: heartbeat: rebalance
messages.note: n1 and n2 learn a rebalance has started and keep processing their partitions meanwhile.

messages.label: JoinGroup (owns p0 p1 p2)
messages.note: Each member reports what it owns, not just that it exists.

messages.label: JoinGroup (owns p3 p4 p5)
messages.note: n1 is the group leader and computes the new plan: 2 partitions each.

messages.label: SyncGroup: give up p2
messages.note: Only the partitions that must move are revoked in this first round.

messages.label: commit p2, stop p2
messages.note: p0 and p1 keep flowing the whole time.

messages.label: SyncGroup: give up p5
messages.note: n2 commits p5's offset and keeps p3 and p4.

messages.label: JoinGroup (second round)
messages.note: Once p2 and p5 are free, a short second round hands them out.

messages.label: assigned p2, p5
messages.note: n3 starts from the committed offsets. Two partitions paused for a moment; four never stopped.

scenarios.name: Alternative: eager
scenarios.summary: The older eager protocol revokes everything from everyone first: a stop-the-world pause for the whole group on every change.

messages.label: JoinGroup
messages.note: Same trigger: a third notifier starts.

messages.label: rebalance
messages.note: Every member must first give up all its partitions.

messages.label: revoke p0 p1 p2
messages.note: Commit and stop all three.

messages.label: revoke p3 p4 p5
messages.note: No passenger in the group gets a message now.

messages.label: JoinGroup (owns nothing)
messages.note: Everyone rejoins empty-handed.

messages.label: assigned p4, p5
messages.note: A fresh plan, which may move more partitions than needed.

messages.label: assigned p0, p1
messages.note: All six partitions paused for the whole rebalance, during a storm, when the group was already behind.

scenarios.name: Notifier 2 crashes
scenarios.summary: A crashed member is noticed when its session expires; its partitions move, and records since its last commit are processed again.

messages.label: process p3: offsets 810–860
messages.note: It sends these messages, then the process is killed before it commits.

messages.label: no heartbeat for session.timeout.ms
messages.note: For the next 45 s p3 and p4 are not consumed by anyone.

messages.label: rebalance: take p3
messages.note: The survivors split n2's partitions.

messages.label: rebalance: take p4
messages.note: n3 keeps p2 and p5; the pause ends when the new owners start.

messages.label: resume p3 at 810
messages.note: The committed offset is 810, so those 50 messages are read again.

messages.label: skip: already sent
messages.note: At-least-once processing: the send log keyed by event id turns the replay into no duplicate SMS.

scenarios.name: Rolling deploy
scenarios.summary: With static membership a member that restarts within the session timeout gets its partitions back, and the deploy causes no rebalance.

messages.label: shutdown: commit, close
messages.note: n1 has a fixed group.instance.id, so it doesn't send LeaveGroup.

messages.label: keep p0, p1 for notifier-1
messages.note: The coordinator waits up to the session timeout before reassigning.

messages.label: JoinGroup as notifier-1
messages.note: The new version is up in about 15 s.

messages.label: same partitions: p0, p1
messages.note: n2 and n3 were never interrupted; only n1's partitions paused, for the length of its restart.
